approach: Retrospective observational study. Cohort: 26 advanced NSCLC patients treated with anti-PD-1 monotherapy, categorized into Responders (PR+SD, n=17) and Non-Responders (PD, n=11), excluding those with recent antibiotic use or other infections. Samples: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) for 16S rRNA sequencing (V3-V4 region) and untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics; paired serum and BALF for LEGENDplex immunoassays of inflammatory cytokines/chemokines; tumor tissues for multiplex immunofluorescence staining (CD4, CD8, CD68, CD206). Analysis: Alpha/Beta diversity metrics, LEfSe for differential taxa, O2PLS and CCA for microbe-metabolite integration, ROC curves for predictive modeling, and correlation analyses linking microbes/metabolites to cytokine levels and immune cell infiltration.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides the first detailed multi-omics landscape (microbiome + metabolome + immune profile) of the lower respiratory tract in advanced NSCLC patients undergoing ICI therapy, identifying specific microbial signatures (Bacillus vs. Sphingomonas/Sediminibacterium) associated with clinical outcomes.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Small sample size (n=26) limits statistical power and generalizability. Retrospective design and single-center origin introduce selection bias. Lack of longitudinal sampling before treatment initiation restricts causal inference regarding microbial changes. Gut microbiome data was not collected, preventing assessment of the lung-gut axis interactions.

key_findings.conditions: Comparing Responders (PR/SD) vs. Non-Responders (PD) in advanced NSCLC.
key_findings.finding: Microbial diversity (beta diversity) significantly differed between groups, with Responders showing distinct community structures. Bacillus was enriched in Responders, while Sphingomonas and Sediminibacterium were associated with Non-Responders.

Responders exhibited metabolic profiles favoring lipid metabolism and essential amino acid degradation pathways linked to beneficial microbes. Non-Responders showed alterations in these pathways associated with pathogenic genera.

Responders had higher infiltration of CD8+ T cells and M1 macrophages (CD68+/CD206-) in tumors. BALF from Responders showed elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, MCP-1, IL-8) compared to Non-Responders, correlating with microbial markers.

A multi-component model combining specific microbes, metabolites, and cytokines (e.g., IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-α2) demonstrated potential for predicting ICI response, though validation is limited by sample size.

problem_or_question: While the gut microbiome's role in ICI response is well-documented, the specific microecological features and predictive value of the lower respiratory tract microbiome in advanced NSCLC remain unclear. This study seeks to determine if local microbial dysbiosis correlates with ICB efficacy and to uncover the underlying metabolic and immune mechanisms.
research_scope: Advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy; focus on lower respiratory tract microbiome and metabolome via bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF).
work_summary: This study investigates the role of the lower respiratory tract microbiome in predicting clinical responses to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in advanced NSCLC. Using a retrospective single-center cohort of 26 patients, the authors performed 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics on BALF samples, alongside cytokine/chemokine assays and multiplex immunohistochemistry on tissue biopsies. The research aims to identify microbial and metabolic signatures associated with treatment outcomes (Partial Response/Stable Disease vs. Progressive Disease) and elucidate the mechanisms by which local microbes influence the tumor immune microenvironment.
